title: An RFQ is never just an RFQ.
shortTitle: An RFQ is never just an RFQ.
description: A B2B electronic components distributor was taking 18 hours to quote in-stock parts and 15 days for out-of-stock ones. I shipped a closed-loop quoting workflow on GPT-3.5 in 2023, then learned the model wasn't the hard part. The data model was.
problem: A B2B electronic components distributor was taking 18 hours to quote in-stock parts and 15 days for out-of-stock ones. I shipped a closed-loop quoting workflow on GPT-3.5 in 2023, then learned the model wasn't the hard part. The data model was.
decision: Automate the full RFQ loop, but route every quote through confidence tiers, price floors, and human override.

sections.label: The Problem
sections.title: Speed was the product, and we were slow.

paragraphs.text: RFQs arrived as unstructured emails. Sales reps looked up part numbers by hand, checked stock, and priced from memory and spreadsheets. In-stock quotes took 18 hours. Out-of-stock quotes took 15 days. In component distribution, response time is a competitive lever, and we were giving it away.

sections.label: The Decision
sections.title: Automate the loop. Keep humans on the edges.

paragraphs.text: In 2023, putting an LLM in front of commercial pricing was a trust problem before it was a technology problem. I designed the workflow so automation handled the routine and people handled the risky, with guardrails deciding which was which.

sections.label: What Went Wrong
sections.title: Our biggest mistake: treating every RFQ as new.

paragraphs.text: Early on, the workflow treated each RFQ as a standalone request. Reality was messier. Follow-ups on existing quotes arrived as brand-new queries. Sister entities of the same customer submitted the same request separately. And the right price depended on context the request never contained: tiered pricing agreements, relationship history, revenue risk, lead time, acceptable alternates, and whether it was a new product introduction or a repeat order.
The fix wasn't a better prompt. It was modeling the account, so every RFQ was read as a moment in a relationship.

sections.label: Outcomes
sections.title: Quotes in under an hour, without giving away the margin.

paragraphs.text: In-stock time to quote went from 18 hours to under 1 hour, and out-of-stock turnaround went from 15 days to under 3. The workflow now handles 8K RFQs a month. Separately, re-architecting shipment tracking and demand forecasting cut logistics costs by 22%.

sections.label: What I Learned
sections.title: The model was the easy part.

paragraphs.text: Automation that ignores the relationship will quote fast and quote wrong. The durable work was in the data model and the guardrails, not the prompt.
